messages:
alex: FYI seeing a perf regression on prod-gpu-9 after the driver bump. seqlen=128 tails are +45% latency, throughput down. any ideas?

maya: Hmm. which kernel path landed? can you paste the probe/log?

raj: logs show fallback to generic_matmul_v1. sample probe output from the node:
```bash
$ ./device_probe --json /dev/nvidia0
{ "sm": 86, "tensor_cores": true, "bf16": true, "fp8": false, "driver": "537.21" }
```

maya: that fp8:false looks wrong — these SM86 cards should report fp8 with our farm drivers. could be nvml quirk or driver ABI change.

sam: i ran a microbench on the same host. short results:
```text
seqlen batch kernel        p50(ms)
128    4     opt_kernel_v3    18.2
128    4     generic_v1       26.5
```
autotuner picked generic_v1 because capability says no fp8, which explains the regression.

tess: note that kv cache warm/cold also flips picks — if kv cold the runtime is more likely to pick safer kernels. but this is clearly a capability flag mismatch.

alex: created a quick canary that forces opt_kernel_v3 on prod-gpu-9 to stop user impact. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1429 :eyes:

infra-bot: PR opened by alex: redwood/infra#1429 (canary kernel override)

raj: proposed permanent fix: augment device probe to (1) query nvmlGetDriverVersion and CUDA runtime, and (2) run a tiny fp8 micro-op verification (single-op matmul) to sanity-check reported fp8 capability. if micro-op passes, mark fp8=true regardless of NVML.

maya: +1. also add metric for device_probe.delta between nvml and micro-op so we can alert on quirking hosts.

bench-bot: ran fp8 micro-op on prod-gpu-9: PASS. micro-op latency 0.9ms, alloc+run completed without fp8 fallback. attached log snippet.

alex: plan of action: (a) land probe + micro-op check (b) re-run autotune on pool (c) roll canary -> rollback schedule and remove override when safe. i'll file follow-ups.

sam: should we also add a soft-autotune heuristic: if newly chosen kernel is >20% worse than baseline for a route, prefer lower-latency choice until fuller validation?

tess: yes — add config flag: runtime.autotune.soft_preference = true and a traced label kernel.choice/kernel.reason. makes postmortem easier.

alex: agreed. i'll add telemetry: trace tags kernel.choice and kernel.reason, and a counter kernel.pick.regression.

maya: also patch the kernel-selection unit tests to simulate nvml mismatch so this doesn't regress again.

alex: filing followups and updating the RFC. thanks all. :thumbsup:
